text:
maria_ae: Heads-up: Lumina POC load test just started returning lots of 5xxs during the ramp. Demo in 25m. Load shows 80-150rps bursts. Can we triage fast?

sylvia_support: Which region/model and any sample errors or request_id?

maria_ae: EU-central (eu-central-1), model=redwood-open-3b-q4-hosted. Error from their harness: 
```
POST /v1/generate
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
x-rw-queue-depth: 57
{"error":"upstream overloaded","request_id":"req_lum_4012"}
```
Also seeing occasional 504s and increased latency.

ben_runtime: Queue depth ~57 -> classic queue saturation. Autoscaler likely behind due to coldstart. Quick mitigation options: 
1) enable API-key scoped failover to 1B variant (instant routing change)
2) set min_replicas=1 for the 3B pool (warmer but costs more)
3) enable per-customer burstpool attach if policy allows (might need approval)

evan_se: Can we do an API-layer soft-failover so quality mostly preserved? Maybe only route >600ms to the smaller model.

ben_runtime: Yes, run: 
```
redwoodctl api-keys update --id key-lumina --set failover_model=redwood-open-1b-q4 --set failover_latency_threshold=600ms
```
That will route slow requests to 1B. Zero infra spin.

sylvia_support: If AE prefers prewarm, whats the cost delta for min_replicas=1 in eu-central? Need a number to tell them.

ben_runtime: Back-of-envelope: min_replicas=1 for 3B in eu-central ~+$720/day. For a 1-hour demo it's ~+$30. I'll confirm exact numbers with finance but those are the quick figures. Fallback approach has near-zero incremental cost for short spikes.

maria_ae: AE also asked about data residency — can we confirm EU logs stay in-region for hosted trials? They might need the wording for legal.

evan_se: Yes, hosted EU customers route logs to eu retention buckets. I'll DM the legal excerpt. If they need a DPA addendum, escalate.

ops-bot: Alert: autoscaler-eu-central spike detected for pool redwood-open-3b-q4 - queue_depth peaked at 61 (alert id A-3123-11).

sylvia_support: I can flip the API key failover now. Maria, keep me posted. Also collect a log bundle for req_lum_4012: `curl -H "x-request-id: req_lum_4012" https://logs.internal/bundle` and metrics: `redwoodctl metrics query --name queue_depth --since 15m --filter customer=lumina`

maria_ae: Done. I flipped failover to 1B with 600ms threshold. Rolling.

ben_runtime: While that's rolling, quick check: are there pending coldstarts? `redwoodctl pools describe redwood-open-3b-q4 --region eu-central-1` will show pending nodes. If pending_coldstarts >0 and queue_depth high, burstpool attach should kick but only if allow_burst=true for the customer.

sylvia_support: I see allow_burst=false for Lumina. Policy default for trials is false unless AE enables it. We can toggle if Lumina agrees. Command: `redwoodctl customers update --id lumina --set allow_burst=true`

maria_ae: Lumina said yes to temporary burst. Please enable and notify them about the small warmup cost.

ops-bot: Action: customer update lumina -> allow_burst=true (deploy d-3123-77).

sylvia_support: After enabling burst and failover, error rate dropped to single digits/min and latency stabilized. Demo team notified and proceeding.

evan_se: Follow-ups to close the loop:
- short AE checklist: request prewarm window or allow API failover for scheduled demos
- doc update: KB entry describing failover commands and cost bullets for trials
- infra: investigate why burstpool auto-attach default is strict for trials (policy vs safety guard)
- perf: explore reducing coldstart prepull for common models to <30s

maria_ae: Demo completed successfully. AE wants to know if we can proactively prewarm next scheduled demo windows. I'll add that to the one-pager.

sylvia_support: I'll create an incident INC-2026-3123-09 for the follow-ups and attach the logs/metrics. Leaving thread open until infra tasks are tracked. :white_check_mark:
